desc: A free-standing elliptical platform centred on the heel keypoint, ground to the ordered plane. The island clears the rim all round; width auto-fits the heel seat and the knobs below resize and reproportion it.
name: Heel post — Oval
params: Height | 0 mm | 0 = fill the bowl without lifting; above 0 the post becomes a platform that raises the heel. | Post angle | 0 ° | Frontal plane: toward medial = varus (thicker medially), toward lateral = valgus. | Heel length | 2.5 × | How far forward the post reaches, as a fraction of the heel seat. | Width scale | 1 × | Scale on the auto-fitted width (rim guard still caps it). | Length / Width | 1.4 × | 0 = auto (fill the heel seat span). Otherwise length = width × this, capped by the seat.
Edge blend | 0 mm | Run over which the post edge fades into the shell. 0 = no blend, a ground edge.
replaces: One heel post per device — enabling Oval removes Flat / U.

desc: A full platform that follows the heel seat’s own outline, held just inside the rim, ground to the ordered plane. The whole rearfoot stands on it.
name: Heel post — Flat
params: Height | 0.5 mm | 0 = fill the bowl without lifting; above 0 the post becomes a platform that raises the heel. | Post angle | 0 ° | Frontal plane: toward medial = varus (thicker medially), toward lateral = valgus. | Heel length | 1.7 × | How far forward the post reaches, as a fraction of the heel seat. | Corner rounding | 1 | Ease the two front corners where the cut edge meets the rim. 0 = as marched, 1 = fully eased.
Edge blend | 0 mm | Run over which the post edge fades into the shell. 0 = no blend, a ground edge.
replaces: One heel post per device — enabling Flat removes Oval / U.

desc: The flat post with its middle left at plain plate thickness: only a U-shaped band around the heel seat’s edge carries the platform. Less material, same seating plane.
name: Heel post — U
params: Height | 0.5 mm | 0 = fill the bowl without lifting; above 0 the post becomes a platform that raises the heel. | Post angle | 0 ° | Frontal plane: toward medial = varus (thicker medially), toward lateral = valgus. | Heel length | 1.6 × | How far forward the post reaches, as a fraction of the heel seat. | Band width | 14 mm | Width of the U’s band itself. 0 = library default; floored at 2 × blend + 4 so both edge blends fit.
Edge blend | 2 mm | Run over which the post edge fades into the shell. 0 = no blend, a ground edge.
replaces: One heel post per device — enabling U removes Oval / Flat.

desc: A block that fills the whole heel seat to the ordered plane and reaches the device edge: no rim guard. The outer wall carries the shell edge straight down the way a full insole body would, and the anterior face is a backward-leaning facet.
name: Heel post — Stabilizer
params: Height | 0.5 mm | 0 = fill the bowl without lifting; above 0 the post becomes a platform that raises the heel. | Post angle | 0 ° | Frontal plane: toward medial = varus (thicker medially), toward lateral = valgus. | Heel length | 1.5 × | How far forward the post reaches, as a fraction of the heel seat. | Wall angle | 10 ° | Inward lean of the outer wall as it descends from the shell edge, degrees from vertical. 0 = straight down.
Front facet run | 0 mm | Run of the anterior facet: the base sits back from the heel-length cut by up to this. 0 = a vertical front face.
replaces: One heel post per device — enabling Stabilizer removes Oval / Flat / U.

desc: Rays fanning from the calcaneal tubercle a full 360° — the plantar fascia’s own load path. Wraps the heel cup unless a post is ordered (then it stops where the post begins).
name: Reinforcement — Radial fan
params: Rib height | 1 mm | Ray count | 26
Rib width | 6 mm
replaces: One reinforcement pattern per device — enabling it removes the others.

desc: Transverse corrugation across the plate — parallel ribs at a fixed pitch, clear of the rim and the distal taper.
name: Reinforcement — Ribbed
params: Rib height | 1.6 mm | Pitch | 8 mm | Crest-to-crest spacing.
Rib width | 6 mm
replaces: One reinforcement pattern per device — enabling it removes the others.

desc: Three rib families 60° apart forming equilateral triangles — the aerospace standard for thin plates, quasi-isotropic so it carries torsion a single direction cannot.
name: Reinforcement — Isogrid
params: Rib height | 1 mm | Cell pitch | 10 mm | Spacing of each family; smaller = denser triangles (heavier plate, bigger STL).
Rib width | 6 mm
replaces: One reinforcement pattern per device — enabling it removes the others.

desc: Four longitudinal ribs under the arch, laid along the navicular line (medialCup → MT1) — the direction the arch actually spans. Lanes shorten toward the insole centre where the vault dies out.
name: Reinforcement — Arch ribs
params: Rib height | 3 mm | Rib length | 90 mm | The border lane’s length; inner lanes shorten from here.
Rib width | 6 mm | Length taper | 0.4 | 0 = all lanes equal · 0.4 = centre-most at 60% of the border lane.
replaces: One reinforcement pattern per device — enabling it removes the others.

desc: A trimline variant: FULL length under ray 1 (the shell itself is the rigid extension under the hallux) while rays 2–5 are cut back to the met line. Built from the toe-fan control points, with a near-vertical split between the rays.
name: Morton’s Extension
params: Split position | 0.6 × | Where the cut runs, as a fraction of the met span from MT1 toward MT5. 0.4 ≈ the gap between ray 1 and ray 2. | Split vertical angle | -5.5 ° | Tilt of the vertical cut. + leans the top toward MT5. | Split horizontal angle | 10 ° | Tilt of the ¾ cut line. + raises the inner corner toward the toes. | Rim start slide | -20 mm | Slide the cut’s start point along the trimline, ± mm in Y from that side’s MT keypoint (MT5 for Morton’s, MT1 for Reverse). + toward the toes.
Edge bevel | 10.5 mm | How far back from the ¾ cut the plantar surface runs down to nothing, so the ledge across the forefoot is not a step. 0 = square edge.
replaces: Owns the distal outline — mutually exclusive with Reverse Morton’s and the plain length settings.

desc: The complement: rays 2–5 keep the full toe length while ray 1 is cut back to the met line — the hallux plantarflexes freely. Same split control as Morton’s.
name: Reverse Morton’s Extension
params: Split position | 0.4 × | Where the cut runs, as a fraction of the met span from MT1 toward MT5. 0.4 ≈ the gap between ray 1 and ray 2. | Split vertical angle | 6.5 ° | Tilt of the vertical cut. + leans the top toward MT5. | Split horizontal angle | 13.5 ° | Tilt of the ¾ cut line. + raises the inner corner toward the toes. | Rim start slide | -20 mm | Slide the cut’s start point along the trimline, ± mm in Y from that side’s MT keypoint (MT5 for Morton’s, MT1 for Reverse). + toward the toes.
Edge bevel | 20 mm | How far back from the ¾ cut the plantar surface runs down to nothing, so the ledge across the forefoot is not a step. 0 = square edge.
replaces: Owns the distal outline — mutually exclusive with Morton’s and the plain length settings.

desc: SHELLS: a ROUND bite out of the MEDIAL side of the front edge — a circle centred on the medial front corner (mt1Trim), so the cut reaches behind the MT line toward the heel. Diameter is the knob. Independent — replaces nothing.
name: 1st Ray Cutout
params: Diameter | 55 % | Diameter of the round bite, as a percentage of the forefoot span. | X position | 7 % | Slide the bite across the foot from the corner (% of the forefoot span). | Y position | 4 % | Slide the bite along the foot from the corner (% of the forefoot span, + toward the toes).

desc: SHELLS: a STRAIGHT oblique cut of the LATERAL side of the front edge — a line set `Depth` inside the lateral front corner (mt5Trim), tilted `Angle` from the MT line, so the cut crosses the MT line toward the heel. Independent — replaces nothing.
name: 5th Ray Cutout
params: Front edge | 40 % | Where the cut leaves the front edge, measured from the lateral corner (% of the forefoot span). | Lateral edge | 14 % | Where the cut meets the lateral edge, measured from the same corner (% of the forefoot span).

desc: An INSOLE with a shortened base: the front edge cut back to the met line and carried distally on one side to block toe-off there, so the foot rolls off over the other side. In-toeing carries the lateral side, out-toeing the medial; the type is chosen per order. All positions are fractions of the forefoot span, so one setting lands on the same anatomy at every size.
name: Gait plate
params: Extension | 18 % | How far past the met line the carried side runs (% of the forefoot span). | Cross-over | 50 % | Where the edge crosses back over, from the carried side (0) to the other (100). 50 puts the change of level between the 2nd and 3rd rays. | Cut-back edge | 0 % | Slide the cut-back contour along the foot: minus toward the heel, plus toward the toes. The carried side never moves with it.
replaces: Mutually exclusive with the ray cutouts — both reshape the same front edge.

desc: A posting slab printed as its OWN part under the insole, so it can carry its own print settings. The medial side is raised and the lateral edge is the hinge, which is varus. Its flat top glues to the insole’s flat underside; the angle lives on its bottom, and that tilted face is what meets the shoe. The insole itself is untouched. Length is Heel to Met Head, Heel to Sulcus, or Heel to End of Toe, chosen in the studio.
name: Medial Wedge
params: Angle | 4 ° | Tilt of the slab across the foot. At 0 no part is made at all.
replaces: One wedge per foot: enabling Medial removes Lateral.

desc: The same slab as the Medial Wedge, raised on the lateral side with the medial edge as the hinge, which is valgus. Its own STL, its own print settings, flat against the insole and tilted toward the shoe.
name: Lateral Wedge
params: Angle | 4 ° | Tilt of the slab across the foot. At 0 no part is made at all.
replaces: One wedge per foot: enabling Lateral removes Medial.

desc: The Heel to Met Head wedge with the angle taken out. The insole is THICKER by a flat height all the way forward to the met heads and thins back over the forefoot past them, so the whole rear of the device sits higher in the shoe while the sole still stands on one flat plane. It is the one raise that is not a separate part: nothing here is angled, so there is nothing to grind and the thickness is simply the insole’s own. No side goes up more than the other; for that, use a wedge. NOT the heel lift, which deepens the seat inside the device and leaves the underside where it was.
name: Thickness boost
params: Height | 4 mm | How much thicker the device is. Held flat all the way to the front edge, then run out over the taper. At 0 nothing is added at all. | Front edge | 0 mm | Slide the edge where the full height stops, from the met heads: minus toward the heel, plus toward the toes. | Taper | 40 mm | How far past that edge the thickness runs out. A STRAIGHT ramp, so the shorter it is the steeper the face.
replaces: One extrinsic raise per foot: this clears the rearfoot post, the forefoot post and the wedge.

desc: SHELLS: a flat facet pressed into the heel from the print-bed side, tilted off it by the ordered angle — an intrinsic rearfoot post without tipping the cup as a whole. Medial inverts the heel, lateral everts it; the side is chosen per order. Independent — replaces nothing.
name: Kirby Skive
params: Depth | 4 mm | How deep the facet is pressed in at its deepest point. | Angle | 5 ° | Tilt of the facet off the bed plane.

desc: Stiffens the MEDIAL wall under the arch: the outer wall angle rises by the amount set here and the rear-wall zone is pulled in to 0.8. No geometry of its own — the studio just switches it on. Independent — replaces nothing.
name: Arch reinforcement
params: Medial wall angle plus | 10 ° | Added to the medial wall angle while this is on.

desc: The heel pad’s sibling under the ARCH: a soft insert on a square-to-circle footprint laid CENTRE ON the Medial High point, clipped to the OUTER trimline (the wall band is inside the soft zone). Top follows the surface; depth reaches down into the thickness. Exported as kind sgarchpad; the autoslicer trims the volume to the insole body. Independent — replaces nothing.

Ignored when Max depth is on. | Max depth | ☑ soft all the way through the floor — the autoslicer trims the volume to the insole body (overrides Depth).

desc: Intrinsic frontal-plane wedge under the HEEL: the whole cup floor tilts about the un-raised edge, which stays put. + = varus (medial side raised), − = valgus (lateral raised). The cup’s outer contour does not move and the floor never rises above the rim, so the cup depth is what limits the angle — the studio slider stops at the limit it measures for each foot. Independent — replaces nothing.
name: Rearfoot posting
params: Varus / Valgus | 4 ° | + = varus (medial up) · − = valgus (lateral up).

desc: Intrinsic post through the trimline: the Medial (varus +) / Lateral (valgus −) Forefoot point rises by tan(angle) × row width and the plantar surface follows the rim through the bed rails. Backward the rim profile dies at the High point; the control rails press the surface back to zero forward (fraction of the arc to the toe apex) and across (fraction of the width). Independent — replaces nothing.

desc: Half-sunk sphere caps on the plantar surface in a fixed 16-bump layout: 5 along the toe contour, two diagonals of 3 down the midfoot, 5 clustered on the heel. Placement is anatomical (met frame + trimline), so the pattern lands the same on every foot; diameter is proportional to insole size. Independent — replaces nothing.

desc: Extra material laid on the heel seat, thickest at the centre and feathering into the surface without a step — the heel pad’s footprint taken the other way (that one cuts a soft insert into the thickness, this one builds the seat up). Its front edge is SHARED with the heel pad (one Front edge knob drives both), it can never stand above the cup’s own rim, and it composes with the heel pad and heel offload. Independent — replaces nothing.

params: Thickness at the centre | 3 mm | How much the centre of the seat gains; the edges get less. | Dish | 20 % | 0 levels the seat into a plane; 100 lifts the cup whole and leaves its full curvature.

desc: A groove cut out of the MEDIAL heel-cup wall — the tarsal tunnel runs behind the medial malleolus — shipped as a NEGATIVE PART (sgheelcut): a 20 mm band that FOLLOWS the wall around the heel, which the slicer subtracts, so the edge stays sharp. It used to be one flat slab, and where the heel curved out of that plane the cut ran out of wall and ended in a step. The insole body itself is untouched; the viewer previews the subtraction. Depth is measured from the rim at each station, length runs along the trimline, the centre can slide toward the toe, and the ends can either bite in hard or fade into the wall. Independent — replaces nothing.

desc: A soft forefoot region the slicer prints at its own density. Its rear boundary is FIVE draggable points in the studio viewer: a point sliding on the LATERAL trimline, an arc through a free mid point (the bow handle) up to the arc/split junction, a line to the corner point, and a line to a point sliding on the MEDIAL trimline. Ships as a through-prism over that footprint (sgkineticwedge), so the slicer owns the region top to bottom — the whole local thickness prints soft, ~4-5 mm over most of the cap. No depth knob: a modifier takes the thickness it finds. Does not change the bed. Independent — replaces nothing.
name: Dannenburg Wedge
